issues.legal_issue: A financial corporation may resort to its direct recovery remedy after obtaining an order through a court-based remedy, provided it abandons the court-based proceedings and does not pursue both remedies simultaneously.
material_facts: A borrower defaulted on a loan, and the corporation obtained an order under the court-based recovery procedure.
The order remained unsatisfied and was not executed; the corporation did not pursue those proceedings further and instead sought recovery through its direct statutory remedy.
The High Court held that obtaining the court order barred the corporation from resorting to the direct remedy.
issues.conclusion: The corporation may resort to the direct recovery remedy after obtaining an unexecuted order, if it abandons the court-based proceedings; it may not pursue both remedies simultaneously. The appeals were allowed and the High Court judgments were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 29 and 31 of the State Financial Corporations Act preserve distinct recovery remedies; Section 31 expressly permits recourse without prejudice to Section 29. Section 32 provides the procedure for implementing orders made under Section 31. The court relied on Gujarat State Financial Corporation v. Naatson Manufacturing Co. (P) Ltd., which held that Section 31 proceedings do not produce a money decree. The doctrine of election does not bar switching between remedies whose scope is essentially different, although simultaneous pursuit is not permitted.

rule.if: financial_recovery_proceeding and court_based_remedy_order_obtained and court_based_remedy_unexecuted and court_based_proceedings_abandoned and not remedies_pursued_simultaneously

predicates.financial_recovery_proceeding: A financial corporation seeks to recover a debt owed by an industrial concern.
predicates.court_based_remedy_order_obtained: The corporation obtained a court order through a court-based recovery procedure.
predicates.court_based_remedy_unexecuted: The corporation did not execute the court order to recover the debt.
predicates.court_based_proceedings_abandoned: The corporation stopped pursuing the court-based proceedings.
predicates.remedies_pursued_simultaneously: The corporation pursued the court-based and direct recovery remedies at the same time.

issues.definition: When a corporation seeking debt recovery has an unexecuted court order and abandons those proceedings without pursuing both remedies simultaneously, it may use the direct recovery remedy.

issues.legal_issue: Equitable writ relief should not be used to protect a persistently defaulting debtor from a corporation’s legitimate recovery action when the debtor’s conduct frustrates recovery.
material_facts: A borrower repeatedly failed to repay the loan or make court-directed deposits and sought stays and other orders that delayed the corporation’s recovery efforts.

After an order obtained through the court-based procedure remained unenforced, the corporation stopped pursuing that remedy and advertised the industrial unit for sale through its direct recovery procedure.
The borrower challenged the renewed sale action in a writ petition, and the High Court’s Division Bench set aside the dismissal of that petition.
issues.conclusion: The borrower was not entitled to equitable writ relief against the corporation’s recovery action; the Division Bench erred, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: In exercising equitable jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, a court should promote honesty and prevent evasion of legitimate rights rather than assist a defaulting party in frustrating recovery. The court also applied the principle that the corporation could abandon the court-based proceedings and use the distinct direct recovery remedy, provided it did not pursue both remedies simultaneously.

rule.if: writ_petition_challenges_creditor_recovery and debtor_persistently_defaulted and debtor_used_delaying_tactics and creditor_abandoned_court_based_proceedings and creditor_invoked_direct_recovery

predicates.writ_petition_challenges_creditor_recove: A debtor filed a writ petition challenging a creditor’s recovery action.
predicates.debtor_persistently_defaulted: The debtor repeatedly failed to repay the debt or comply with court-directed payment requirements.
predicates.debtor_used_delaying_tactics: The debtor used litigation or requests for relief that delayed the creditor’s recovery efforts.
predicates.creditor_abandoned_court_based_proceedin: The creditor stopped pursuing the court-based recovery proceedings.
predicates.creditor_invoked_direct_recovery: The creditor used a direct procedure to recover the debt from the debtor’s property.

issues.definition: If a debtor persistently defaults and uses delaying tactics while challenging a creditor’s direct recovery action in a writ petition, and the creditor has abandoned its court-based proceedings, equitable writ relief should not shield the debtor from legitimate recovery.
